column1: # Accepted differences between the port and the original Sim68K core
# Each is an undefined result or a bug of the original that the port fixes.

column3: N and V are undefined (PRM); the original inverts them (cc_update UND), the port sets N from the result and leaves V
Z, V, C are undefined (PRM); the original inverts them (cc_update UND), the port leaves them unchanged
overflow: C must be cleared (PRM), the original leaves it unchanged (bug, fixed); N and Z are undefined
V must be cleared (PRM); the original computes it with the ASL overflow rule (cc_update CASE_9; bug, fixed)

address/bus error: the original raises the exception inside the memory access after (An)+/-(An) updates and EA cycles; the port restores the registers, condition codes and cycle count of the instruction start; the original also carries on after the failed access (e.g. computes flags from it)
exception frames stack the SR, which holds the undefined flags above

the original reads the MOVE destination before writing it (eff_addr() for the destination EA; the 68000 does not), so a faulting destination stacks a read (R/W=1) frame with the read PC; the port stacks a write frame (bug, fixed)
ADDQ.B/SUBQ.B #n,An is illegal on the 68000; the original executes it as .L (CODE3.CPP; bug, fixed)
BCHG/BCLR/BSET Dn with d16(PC), d8(PC,Xn) or #imm is illegal on the 68000; the original accepts any data mode (BIT_OP; bug, fixed)

MOVE to d16(PC)/d8(PC,Xn)/#imm is illegal; the original reads the source before checking the destination mode, so a faulting source raises an address error instead (the 68000 rejects the encoding first)
MOVE to SR with an invalid EA in user mode: the original checks privilege before decoding the EA; the encoding is illegal first
BFCHG/BFCLR/BFSET/BFINS need a control alterable EA (68020); the original accepts d16(PC)/d8(PC,Xn) (BIT_FIELD; bug, fixed)

illegal encoding: the original fetches and updates operands (e.g. (An)+, -(An), extension words, EA cycles) before it rejects the encoding; the port rejects it first, as the 68000 does, so registers, cycles and the frame position (SSP) are those of the instruction start
byte ABCD/SBCD/ADDX/SUBX -(A7) and CMPM (A7)+: the original steps A7 by 1, leaving the stack pointer odd; the 68000 steps A7 by 2 (bug, fixed)
BCHG/BCLR/BSET #n with d16(PC), d8(PC,Xn) or #imm is illegal on the 68000; the original accepts any data mode and writes into the program (BIT_OP; bug, fixed)
ORI/ANDI/EORI to CCR use the low byte of the immediate word only; the original applies the whole word, changing the system byte of SR (bug, fixed; assembled code always has a zero high byte)
ASL/ASR with a count register: the original's V test for large counts has an operator-precedence bug (cc_update CASE_4 `shiftCount > (size-1) & source`); the port sets V per the PRM
illegal bit field encodings: the original fetches the extension word before rejecting the encoding, so its illegal-instruction frame stacks PC+2 (see the @illegal rule)
